title: The Model Was Right. The Harness Failed. — Vinoth Govindarajan, OpenAI
talk_summary: Vinoth Govindarajan argues that most production agent failures are harness failures, not model failures, using OpenClaw issues as case studies. He prescribes a contract: the model proposes, the harness commits, and a receipt proves the action, organized around owning state, ordering mutations, bounding work, constraining authority, and preserving evidence.

takeaways.technique: Single ordered commit path per mutable state boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: They identify load-modify-save races where two callers overwrite each other's changes, and require one ordered commit path (queue, mutex, transaction, or lock) per mutable state boundary, while still allowing parallel reads and fan-out.
takeaways.evidence_quote: One ordered commit path for one mutable state boundary.

takeaways.technique: Run receipts with terminal outcomes and deadlines
takeaways.what_they_do: They require every run to have a deadline, watchdog, and a recorded terminal outcome (success, failure, timeout, cancel, max attempts) so a run never waits forever on an event that cannot arrive, and recovery commands don't queue behind stuck work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every external boundary needs an ending. Success, failure, timeout, cancel, or max attempts.

takeaways.technique: Scoped approval objects bound to action, arguments, and lifetime
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat approval as a scoped execution state, not a vague memory: an approval object records who approved, in what session/run, for which tool and arguments, for how long, and with what outcome, and expiration terminates rather than loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Approval as a scoped execution state, it must stay bound to the action it authorized.

takeaways.technique: Five-question receipt audit per production path
takeaways.what_they_do: They prescribe auditing one real production trace with five questions: what woke it up, what state it inherited, which authority it used, what executed, and what evidence survived at the user-visible edge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: What woke it up? What state did it inherit? Which authority did it use? What executed? And what evidence survived?

takeaways.technique: Verify at the user-visible edge, not internal success
takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish internal tool success from external proof: a tool reporting success only proves the request was accepted, not that the user-visible surface confirmed it; the receipt must end at the boundary that matters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Internal success is not external proof.

takeaways.technique: Explicit working-set assembly with named state owners
takeaways.what_they_do: They note the model is stateless and the harness rebuilds the working set each turn (transcript, session state, memory, policy, tool definitions); for every fact the agent may reuse, name the owner and the replay path, since coherence does not prove completeness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The model only sees what the harness supplies. If one input is missing or stale, the answer may still sound coherent.
